extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (practitioners handling national-stage and reexamination proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for assessing unity of invention, formal defects, election/restriction requirements in national-stage (35 U.S.C. 371) applications, and procedural/ substantive criteria for ex parte reexamination proceedings. Includes Markush-group rules, drawing/description/claim defect standards, and reexamination SNQ rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for unity of invention (37 CFR 1.475(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. The requirement is fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among those inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression 'special technical features' means those technical features that define a contribution which each of the claimed inventions, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art. The determination is made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim (see 37 CFR 1.475(e)). Begin lack-of-unity actions in national-stage applications with the specified heading and follow with the appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 18.19 or 18.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of unity without regard to claim format (37 CFR 1.475(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether a group of inventions is so linked as to form a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let claim drafting format (separate claims vs alternatives within a single claim) dictate unity; analyze technical features and contribution over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted combinations of different categories of invention (37 CFR 1.475(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application containing claims to different categories of invention will be considered to have unity of invention if the claims are drawn only to one of these combinations: (1) product & process specially adapted for manufacture of that product; (2) product & process of use of that product; (3) product, process specially adapted for manufacture, and a use; (4) process & apparatus/means specifically designed for carrying out the process; (5) product, process specially adapted for manufacture, and apparatus/means specifically designed for carrying out the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims fall outside these permitted combinations, unity may not be present (see 37 CFR 1.475(c)). When making restriction requirements between product/apparatus and process, follow guidance about rejoinder (form paragraph 8.21.04) and reconsider restriction if elected claims are allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping claims in lack-of-unity actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs provide templates for enumerating groups of claims (e.g., 'Group [1], claim(s) [2], drawn to [3]') used when claims are directed to multiple products, processes, uses, or apparatuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert Roman numerals for groups, respective claim numbers, and names of grouped inventions. Use 18.06, 18.06.01, 18.06.02 as appropriate to indicate two, three, or an additional group(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of same or corresponding technical feature among groups
rubrics_metrics.description: [1] lack unity of invention because the groups do not share the same or corresponding technical feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims of different groups are directed to different combinations of features (example: Group I directed to A+B, Group II to C+D). For international phase or U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 identify groups by Roman numerals or species per form paragraph instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared technical feature does not constitute a special technical feature
rubrics_metrics.description: [1] lack unity of invention because even though the inventions of these groups require the technical feature of [2], this technical feature is not a special technical feature as it does not make a contribution over the prior art in view of [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 identify the technical feature; in bracket 3 cite prior art showing the feature does not contribute; in bracket 4 explain how the shared feature lacks novelty or inventive step. Whether a feature makes a 'contribution' is considered with respect to novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-group chemical alternatives: criteria for 'similar nature'
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single claim defines alternatives of a Markush group, the alternatives are regarded as being of a similar nature where (A) all alternatives have a common property or activity; AND (B) (1) a common structure is present (a significant structural element is shared by all alternatives); OR (B)(2) if common structure cannot unify, all alternatives belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Significant structural element’ refers to a common chemical structure occupying a large portion of structures, or a small but structurally distinctive portion essential to the common property in view of prior art. ‘Recognized class’ means expectation from the art that members will behave similarly and be substitutable one for another to achieve the intended result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush alternatives lack common property or activity (18.07.03a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chemical compounds of [1] are not regarded as being of similar nature because all of the alternatives do not share a common property or activity. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the groups/species and explain which property/activity is missing. For national stage, identify species per form paragraph instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush alternatives share common structure but structure not significant and not in recognized class (18.07.03b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the chemical compounds of [1] share a common structure of [2], the common structure is not a significant structural element because it represents only a small portion of the compound structures and does not constitute a structurally distinctive portion in view of [3]. Further, the compounds do not belong to a recognized class. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 identify the common structure; in bracket 3 cite prior art showing lack of distinctiveness; in bracket 4 explain why not a recognized class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush alternatives do not share common structure or belong to recognized class (18.07.03c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chemical compounds of [1] are not regarded as being of similar nature because: (1) all the alternatives do not share a common structure and (2) the alternatives do not all belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert reasoning. For national stage identify groups/species as directed by earlier form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing is required (PCT Article 7(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter of this application admits of illustration by drawing to facilitate understanding of the invention. Applicant is required under PCT Article 7(1) to furnish a drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert specific identification of required drawings in bracket 1. Use when drawings are necessary for understanding; follow with drawing-related form paragraphs (e.g., 18.08.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing objections — lack of clarity (PCT Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings are objected to under PCT Article 7 as lacking clarity under PCT Article 7 because: [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert reasons why drawings lack clarity (e.g., inaccurate showing). Identify specific defects in drawings in the bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description defect — inadequate written description (PCT Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The application, as originally filed, did not describe: [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claim(s) and the subject matter not described in the application as filed. Use to object if claims claim matter not originally described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description defect — non-enabling disclosure (PCT Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The description does not disclose the claimed invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the claimed invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art as required by PCT Article 5 because: [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify claimed subject matter not enabled and explain why it is not enabled. Insert relevant details in bracket 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description defect — failure to disclose best mode (PCT Rule 5.1(a)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The description fails to set forth the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the claimed invention as required by PCT Rule 5.1(a)(v) because: [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify claim(s), verb forms, and insert the objection and reasons in bracket 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — defect in form or contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contain(s) the following defect(s) in the form or contents thereof: [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pluralize 'claim' if needed and identify the technical deficiency in bracket 2 (e.g., antecedent basis, indefiniteness, formal defects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims objectionable — indefiniteness (PCT Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 as lacking clarity because claim [2] indefinite for the following reason(s): [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert specific reasons for indefiniteness in bracket 3. Ensure claim numbering and verb forms are correct in brackets 1 and 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement in national stage (35 U.S.C. 121, 372; 37 CFR 1.499)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application contains inventions or groups of inventions which are not so linked as to form a single general inventive concept under PCT Rule 13.1. In accordance with 37 CFR 1.499, applicant is required, in reply to this action, to elect a single invention to which the claims must be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 18.19 when making a restriction requirement in a national stage application. Follow with form paragraphs 18.06 - 18.06.02 and 18.07 - 18.07.02 as appropriate. Notify applicant of election requirement and, for product/process restrictions, include rejoinder guidance (form paragraph 8.21.04). Reconsider restriction if elected claims become allowable to verify non-elected claims do not share a same or corresponding technical feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species in national stage (18.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application contains claims directed to more than one species of the generic invention. These species are deemed to lack unity of invention because they are not so linked as to form a single general inventive concept under PCT Rule 13.1. Applicant is required to elect a single species to which the claims shall be restricted if no generic claim is finally held to be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply must identify the claims readable on the elected species; an argument that a claim is allowable or that all claims are generic is non-responsive unless accompanied by an election. Upon allowance of a generic claim, applicant is entitled to consideration of additional species written in dependent form or requiring all limitations of an allowed generic claim. Identify species in bracket 1 and each generic claim by number or insert 'NONE'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by original presentation and withdrawal of nonelected claims (18.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly submitted claim [1] directed to an invention that lacks unity with the invention originally claimed for the following reasons: [2]. Since applicant has received an action on the merits for the invention originally presented and constructively elected by original presentation for prosecution on the merits, claim [3] [is] withdrawn from consideration as being directed to a nonelected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when newly submitted claims are nonelected by original presentation; identify the new claim and reasons and indicate withdrawal per 37 CFR 1.142(b) and MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for election and rules for traversal (37 CFR 1.143; right to petition 1.144)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply must include (i) an election of a species or invention to be examined even though the requirement may be traversed (37 CFR 1.143) and (ii) identification of the claims encompassing the elected invention. The election may be made with or without traverse. To preserve a right to petition, the election must be made with traverse. If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement, the election shall be treated as an election without traverse. Traversal must be presented at the time of election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If traversing on the ground that inventions have unity, applicant must provide reasons and may submit evidence or identify evidence of obvious variants or admissions. Evidence or admissions provided may be used by the examiner in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) of the other invention. Failure to timely traverse results in loss of right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144. If claims are added after election, applicant must indicate which are readable on the elected invention or species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination program — filing & timing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the accelerated examination program is to complete examination within twelve months from filing date. Any reply must be filed electronically via EFS-Web; if not filed electronically the final disposition may occur later than twelve months. No extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be permitted for applications with special status under the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph when requiring restriction in an application that entered national stage and is under accelerated examination. Emphasize electronic filing and the lack of extensions under 1.136(a) for such applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: New question of patentability in reexamination (SNQ) — notice (22.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial new question of patentability affecting claim [1] of United States Patent Number [2] is raised by the request for ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in orders granting reexamination or Office actions raising a ground of rejection. In reexamination proceedings, explain the SNQ basis and insert relevant citations and explanation as to why the SNQ exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for applying old art as sole basis for reexamination (22.01.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on previously cited/considered patents and/or printed publications ('old art') does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability. Determinations are based on a fact-specific inquiry case-by-case; old art presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way (e.g., due to new argument/interpretation) can establish an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When old art is used as the sole basis, insert the old art in bracket 2 and explain how/why that fact situation applies in bracket 3 (e.g., different way of viewing art, material new argument). This paragraph is used the first time the already-cited art is applied; do not repeat for same art in subsequent Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substantial new question of patentability (22.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: No substantial new question of patentability is raised by the request for reexamination and prior art cited therein for the reasons set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reexamination request does not present an SNQ; explain reasons why not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue not within scope of ex parte reexamination (22.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue has been raised in the present reexamination proceeding that is not within the scope of an ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304. [1]. This issue will not be considered in the present proceeding. 37 CFR 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify issues (e.g., public use, on-sale, conduct, abandonment) that are outside the scope; do not independently raise such issues as an examiner in reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers to be submitted in response to Office action in reexamination (22.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits, declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action. Submissions after the next Office action (intended to be final) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116 after final rejection and 37 CFR 41.33 after appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage prompt submission of evidence or amendments in response to the current Office action to ensure consideration; late submissions are strictly governed and may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in reexamination proceedings (22.04.01 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in reexamination proceedings because those provisions apply only to 'an applicant'. 35 U.S.C. 305 and 37 CFR 1.550(a) require reexamination proceedings to be conducted with special dispatch. Extensions of time in ex parte reexamination are provided for in 37 CFR 1.550(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that extensions are limited and specify applicable regulations for requesting extensions (37 CFR 1.550(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceedings based on reissue claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue patent has surrendered the original patent, all subsequent proceedings in this reexamination will be based on the reissue patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert original patent and reissue patent numbers and effective date; use when reexamination is triggered by reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation reminder — duty to apprise Office (37 CFR 1.565(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is reminded of the continuing responsibility under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to apprise the Office of any litigation activity, or other prior or concurrent proceeding, involving Patent No. [1] throughout the course of this reexamination proceeding. The third party requester may also apprise the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in first action when granting ex parte reexamination request or Director-ordered reexamination. Cite MPEP sections for further guidance (e.g., §§ 2207, 2282, 2286).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and shortened statutory period in reexamination actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action is made final in reexamination (including actions necessitated by amendment), a shortened statutory period for response is set (normally TWO MONTHS). Filing a timely first response will be construed as including a request to extend the shortened period for an additional two months; in no event will the statutory period expire later than SIX MONTHS from mailing date of final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply in reexamination; requests for extensions must follow reexamination-specific rules and fees under 37 CFR 1.17(g). Final Office actions must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 305 — claim enlarges scope of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305 as enlarging the scope of the claim(s) of the patent being reexamined. A claim enlarges the scope where it is broader than any claim of the patent. A claim is broader if it contains any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent; broadened if broader in any one respect even if narrower in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claim limitations considered to broaden the scope and explain why (insert in bracket 2). See MPEP § 2258 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendments in reexamination must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and formal presentation (37 CFR 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the specification and/or claims in this reexamination proceeding must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), must be formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and must contain any fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise patent owner of proper manner of making amendments in a reexamination proceeding; use in order granting reexamination and/or first Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment in an ex parte reexamination — correction required (22.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] proposes amendments to [2] that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). A supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments in the present ex parte reexamination proceeding is required. Failure to timely correct this informality will result in the amendment being held not to be an appropriate response, termination of prosecution of the present ex parte reexamination proceeding, and issuance of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set a shortened statutory period for response (normally TWO MONTHS). After final rejection, an improper amendment should not be entered and patent owner informed using Form PTOL 467.
